result.summary: I rebuilt every metric from the raw CSVs without using hitung.py or hitung2.py, with my own stdlib point-in-polygon (Polygon and MultiPolygon, holes handled). All 160 values in angka.json match mine exactly (8 provinces x 5 metrics x 4 days, max abs diff 0). That covers WIB day assignment, the 07:00 WIB cut-off, the confidence filters, the 0.978 weight, the 3x3 neighbourhood, the Chebyshev<=4 clustering for fs, and province assignment. fs only matches if N21 cells are included, which is what the spec says ('VIIRS n/h cells'). The raw files contain no duplicate detections. Each file holds exactly one acq_date, the one in its name, and no (sat, lat, lon, date, time) key appears twice. The deck also matches my recomputation: all 72 table numbers, all totals rows, subtitle 1 (5.097 / 49 persen / 10.332 / 5.235), subtitle 2 (8.486) and the FS pills (955 / 962 / 817). One real problem is in the input data: the Suomi-NPP daytime overpass over central and western Indonesia on 20 Oct is missing from the raw file, so the 20 Oct numbers come out too low (and padam(20) probably too high). Two smaller presentation issues: arrows are calculated from unrounded values, and a value already rounded to 1 decimal is rounded again, which leaves a few displayed numbers 1 ha off. Scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alfatehanseptianta-Documents-GitHub-poskokarhutla/519b7abb-b696-465e-bd1c-bcbbfb8815f9/scratchpad/verif/ (verif.py, verif_raw.py, extra.py, deck.py; outputs mine.json and mine_raw.json).

findings.what: The input data is missing a satellite pass. The Suomi-NPP (N) daytime overpass of WIB 20 Oct over about 100-131E is absent from VIIRS_SNPP_NRT-20.csv. Every 20 Oct value that uses N (hot, luas, belum, and cells[20], which feeds padam(20)) is therefore too low for Kalimantan, Sumatra and Sulawesi. Because fewer day-20 cells exist, more day-19 points find no neighbour, so padam(20) is probably too high. The spec was implemented correctly; the source file is incomplete.
findings.evidence: SNPP granules per UTC day: on 18 Oct, 06:22 and 06:25 UTC cover lon 101.4-124.7 (3,782 rows). On 19 Oct, 06:01, 06:03 and 06:05 cover 101.5-126.9. On 20 Oct the only daytime granules are 04:02-04:06 UTC, covering lon 131-142 (385 rows), and nothing at 05-06 UTC. By the 07:00 WIB cut-off that pass was about 18 hours old. Count of N n/h detections in daytime, WIB day, west of 119E: 17 Oct 1,513, 18 Oct 3,246, 19 Oct 1,279, 20 Oct 0. In the same area NOAA-20 daytime on 20 Oct still has 2,355, so fires were burning. Ratio of N to N20 n/h by province (18 Oct vs 20 Oct): Kalteng 4,564:4,805 vs 340:1,558; Kalsel 496:279 vs 63:567; Kaltim 661:357 vs 56:426; Papua Selatan 875:1,353 vs 284:1,573. Headline values affected include Kalteng luas 20 Okt 4.007 (▼55%), hot 2.363 (▼44%), belum 3.052, and the subtitle '±5.097 ha (49 persen) ... telah padam'. Recommend re-downloading SNPP 20 Oct, or confirming an SNPP outage, before reading the 20 Oct drops as real.

findings.what: Arrows are calculated from unrounded (1-decimal) values, not from the integers shown. In 10 of 72 cells, recomputing from the displayed numbers gives a percentage 1-6 points different. Every one of the 10 matches exactly when unrounded values are used, so the code is consistent; only the reader-facing arithmetic differs.
findings.evidence: Shown vs recomputed from displayed integers: Sumsel belum 20 Okt ▲97% vs ▲98% (581 -> 1.148). Kalsel belum 18 Okt ▲908% vs ▲904%. Jambi luas 18 Okt ▲719% vs ▲722%, luas 20 Okt ▲67% vs ▲68%, belum 18 Okt ▲12% vs ▲11%, belum 20 Okt ▲71% vs ▲72% (47 -> 81). Sulteng luas 18 Okt ▲346% vs ▲347%, belum 18 Okt ▲370% vs ▲376%. Kaltim belum 18 Okt ▲568% vs ▲567%, belum 20 Okt ▼53% vs ▼52% (991 -> 471). A reader can only check the 19 and 20 Oct arrows, because 17 Oct is not printed. All arrow colours are correct (D9600B for ▲, 2F86D1 for ▼).

findings.what: Double rounding. angka.json stores 1-decimal values, and those are rounded again to integers (Python's round-half-to-even on x.5). Four exact values cross a .5 boundary; two of them reach the deck.
findings.evidence: Kalteng belum 19 Okt: exact 7916.528 is stored as 7916.5 and displayed as 7.916; it should be 7.917. That makes Jumlah 5 provinsi belum 19 Okt 10.820 (should be 10.821) and Jumlah 8 provinsi 14.324 (should be 14.325). Kalsel padam 20 Okt: exact 1125.478 is stored as 1125.5 and rounded to 1126, so subtitle 1 P = 5.097 and P+B = 10.332 should be 5.096 and 10.331. Q stays 49%. Kalteng padam 18 Okt (968.532) and Kalbar padam 18 Okt (134.504) are also affected but are not displayed. Each error is 1 ha.

findings.what: Checked raw-file overlap and duplicates: none found. Province clipping loses little.
findings.evidence: After the cut-off filter, 153,886 rows, with 0 repeated (satellite, lat, lon, acq_date, acq_time) keys. Each file contains only its own UTC acq_date. Only 3 lat/lon pairs repeat across all files, and each pair is two different detections (different satellite or date, e.g. N20 17 Oct 18:04 vs N20 18 Oct 17:45 at -2.89953, 111.57457). For 18-20 Oct, of 60,268 N/N20/MODIS points, 146 fall inside an 8-province bounding box but in no province polygon (117 of them near Papua Selatan, likely offshore or across the PNG border). That is negligible.

result.summary:
The code matches the spec exactly. The deck numbers are a faithful copy of angka.json except for a few off-by-one roundings. The real problems are a data gap and some method differences from the platform's own standards.

Code vs spec:
- I wrote a separate implementation from the spec (verif/audit/a1.py). It reproduced all 160 values in angka.json (8 provinces × hot/luas/belum/padam/fs × 17–20 Oct) with 0 mismatches.
- The raw input is clean:
  - 26 files, 157,488 rows, 0 duplicates; every acq_date matches its file's date.
  - Satellite codes are N/N20/N21/Terra/Aqua; VIIRS confidence is l/n/h and MODIS confidence is numeric.
  - UTC+7 and the cut-off (21 Oct 07:00 WIB = 21 Oct 00:00 UTC) are applied on both the hotspot path and the VIIRS path.
  - Hotspot counts take M+N+N20 at all confidence levels. Cells and luas take n/h detections only.
- Day indexing is right: belum compares day-d points against cells[d-1]; padam compares day-(d-1) points against cells[d]. FS clustering (Chebyshev distance ≤ 4 cells) matches an independent union-find.
- The 8 target polygons have no holes, no repeated codes, and 0 points fall in two provinces, so using outer rings only does no harm here.

Final PPTX (a4.py):
- All 72 values, arrows (sign, % and colour D9600B/2F86D1), bar colours and bar heights are correct. Bar height is max(18288, H·v/max), anchored at the row base.
- Totals rows (5 provinces; 3 and 8 provinces), FS pills (955/962/817) and subtitles (5.097 / 49 / 10.332 / 5.235; 8.486) are consistent with angka.json.
- Row order is right, no template numbers or "NA" are left over, and there are no duplicate shape ids.
- The hotspot definition matches the platform's (laporan.py and harian.py SENSOR_UTAMA = M, N, N20, all confidence, WIB calendar day; kumulatif.json 'definisi'). With the platform's kecamatan polygons, the WIB-calendar count gives 2.619/2.632/2.766 for Papua Selatan, against 2.618/2.632/2.766 in the original BNPB template. The deck itself shows 2.617/2.631/2.763 because it uses the simplified provinsi.json polygons.

Main problems:
1. **S-NPP data gap on 20 Oct.** The S-NPP daytime overpass is missing from the data on 20 Oct, and the luas formula halves the S-NPP share when it is absent. This pulls down the 20 Oct numbers and some of the 19→20 arrows.
2. **"Telah padam" breaks the platform rule.** The deck calls fires extinguished after one day without detection. The platform keeps a fire active until 72 hours without detection (168 hours on dry peat), and treats a 24-hour gap as possibly clouds or smoke.
3. **Slide 1 subtitle mixes two days.** The burned-out area is measured on 19 Oct detections and the still-burning area on 20 Oct detections, so the 10.332 ha total is not the active area of any one day.
4. **Luas differs from the platform method and is not disclosed.** The deck averages S-NPP and NOAA-20 with no method note on the slide; the platform uses S-NPP only.

Smaller issues:
- Double rounding (one decimal first, then Python's round-half-to-even) gives off-by-one values.
- The kept template sentence "karena peningkatan hotspot" contradicts the deck's own Kaltim numbers.
- About 5–9% of BELUM PADAM rests only on detections less than 12 hours apart across WIB midnight.
- The grid cell and polygon source differ slightly from the platform's (each effect ≤ 1%).

Scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alfatehanseptianta-Documents-GitHub-poskokarhutla/519b7abb-b696-465e-bd1c-bcbbfb8815f9/scratchpad/verif/audit/ (a1–a8.py, mine_exact.json). No existing files were modified.

findings.what: The S-NPP daytime overpass for 20 Oct (WIB) is missing from the raw FIRMS data. hitung2.py rata() always divides by 2 and has no gap handling, so the 20 Oct LUAS and BELUM PADAM values (the headline day) are biased low. Several 19→20 arrows change direction once a single satellite is used for both days. The platform documents a gap fill for days without S-NPP (laporan.py isi_celah; NOAA-20 ×0,978 substitution in luas_banding), but nothing here detects or discloses the gap.
findings.evidence:
S-NPP daytime rows at all confidence levels: 18 Oct 6,131; 19 Oct 5,268; 20 Oct only 385, all at 04 UTC over lon 131–142. There are no 05–07 UTC granules on 20 Oct, while 19 Oct had 2,102 at 06 UTC.

S-NPP n/h daytime detections on 20 Oct = 0 in 7 of 8 provinces (Kalteng: N day 0, N20 day 929).

Using NOAA-20 ×0,978 alone on both days (unaffected by the gap), 19→20 Oct:
- Kalsel luas: deck ▼38%, NOAA-20 +16%.
- Papua Selatan luas: deck ▼19%, NOAA-20 +38%.
- Papua Selatan belum: deck ▼12%, NOAA-20 +20%.
- Kaltim luas: deck ▼30%, NOAA-20 −3%.

Hotspot counts without S-NPP (M+N20), 19→20 Oct:
- Kalsel: deck ▼6%, M+N20 +86%.
- Papua Selatan: deck ▲5%, M+N20 +97%.
- Kaltim: deck ▲9%, M+N20 +58%.

Kalteng luas 20 Oct: deck 4,007 ha; NOAA-20 ×0,978 alone 6,552 ha. (a2.py, a3.py, a5.py)

findings.what: The slide 1 subtitle says "±5.097 ha ... api aktif telah padam pada 20 Okt", based on one day without detection. That contradicts the platform's own rule. harian.py:27-30 and 411 keep a fire complex active while it was detected within 72 h (168 h on dry peat, DC > 350), and harian.py:444 defines teramati=False (no detection for 24 h) as "bisa padam, bisa tertutup awan/asap". The missing S-NPP pass on 20 Oct also makes cells[20] sparser, which pushes padam up further.
findings.evidence: At cut-off (21 Oct 07:00 WIB), any detection from 19 Oct WIB is at most 55 h old. Under the platform's 72 h / 168 h rule, 0 ha would qualify as padam, against the deck's 5.097 ha. ganti.py:91-95 writes padam(20 Oct) from hitung2.py:46 (19 Oct points with no 3×3 neighbour in cells[20]).

findings.what: The slide 1 subtitle percentage mixes two days. P (padam) is measured on 19 Oct detections and B (belum) on 20 Oct detections, so P+B = 10.332 ha is not the active fire area of any single day. Measured on one consistent base, P plus the 19 Oct points still seen on 20 Oct equals exactly LUAS 19 Oct.
findings.evidence:
5 provinces, exact values:
- padam20 = 5,095.6 ha.
- 19 Oct points still seen on 20 Oct = 8,370.7 ha; padam20 plus this = 13,466.3 ha = luas19.
- belum20 = 5,234.0 ha.

Deck Q = P/(P+B) = 49.3% (shown as 49 persen). Same-base share P/luas19 = 37.8%. Neither luas19 (13.467) nor luas20 (7.878) equals the deck's 10.332. (a5.py)

findings.what: The LUAS TERBAKAR and BELUM PADAM formula differs from the platform standard. The platform computes luas = VIIRS S-NPP n/h × 4,3 ha (laporan.py docstring line 8, hitung() lines 80-83, seri() line 99, sumber.luas). NOAA-20 ×0,978 is only a substitute for days with no S-NPP data (luas_banding.sumber[perkiraan].metode). The deck instead averages (N + 0,978·N20)/2 × 4,3. The slide does not disclose this. ganti.py:102 defines a method note (CAT) that is never inserted, so the asterisks on LUAS TERBAKAR*/BELUM PADAM* point to "*Data berdasarkan GIS (Geographic Information System)." The platform's caveat that daily and per-province figures are only indicative is also missing. CAT itself says "VIIRS S-NPP ... 4,3 ha per titik", which would misdescribe the averaged formula.
findings.evidence:
LUAS per province, 18/19/20 Oct — deck (averaged) vs platform (S-NPP only):
- Kalteng: 19.916 / 8.918 / 4.007 vs 19,625 / 5,173 / 1,462.
- Jambi: 707 / 103 / 173 vs 228 / 194 / 206.
- Kalsel: 1.653 / 2.133 / 1.328 vs 2,133 / 2,206 / 271.
- Kaltim: 2.172 / 1.458 / 1.016 vs 2,842 / 1,066 / 241.
- Papua Selatan: 4.726 / 4.820 / 3.918 vs 3,762 / 4,855 / 1,221.

The slide text reads "LUAS TERBAKAR*" with the footnote "*Data berdasarkan GIS (Geographic Information System)." (a1.py, a4.py)

findings.what: Double rounding causes off-by-one displayed values. hitung2.py:44-46 stores round(x, 1); ganti.py:4/74/90 then applies Python round(), which rounds halves to even. Exact values just above or below .5 therefore round the wrong way under any rounding convention.
findings.evidence:
Kalteng BELUM 19 Okt: exact 7,916.528 is stored as 7916.5 and shown as 7.916; correct is 7.917. This carries into:
- Slide 1 "Jumlah 5 provinsi" BELUM 19 Okt: 10.820 → should be 10.821.
- Slide 2 "Jumlah 8 provinsi" BELUM 19 Okt: 14.324 → should be 14.325.

Kalsel padam 20 Okt: exact 1,125.478 is stored as 1125.5 and used as 1,126; correct is 1,125. So the subtitle shows ±5.097 ha (should be 5.096) and ±10.332 ha (should be 10.331). Q stays 49%.

findings.what: Slide 2 keeps the template sentence "3 provinsi tambahan masuk prioritas karena peningkatan hotspot." The deck's own numbers do not support it for Kaltim, and only partly for Papua Selatan.
findings.evidence: Kaltim hotspot: 1.107 → 697 (▼37%) → 758 (▲9%); net −32% from 18 to 20 Oct. Papua Selatan 18 Okt: ▼25%. Only Sulteng rises steadily (217 → 442 → 905).

findings.what: The "bertahan ≥1 hari" test behind BELUM PADAM and FS can be met by detections only about an hour apart. The Kalimantan night overpass straddles WIB midnight, so a 23:xx WIB detection on d-1 and a 00:xx WIB detection on d count as persisting. FS is also defined differently from the platform's fire complex (kompleks: DBSCAN 1.5 km, 7-day window, active ≤ 72 h), so 955/962/817 FS is not the platform's complex count.
findings.evidence:
NOAA-20 n/h on 18 Oct: 2,519 at 16 UTC (23:xx WIB) and 4,555 at 17 UTC (00:xx WIB 19 Oct).

8-province BELUM when the d-1 neighbour must be ≥ 12 h earlier:
- 18 Okt: 22,846 → 21,079 ha (92% kept).
- 19 Okt: 14,326 → 13,096 ha (91%).
- 20 Okt: 8,484 → 8,065 ha (95%).

For scale, public/data/kluster.json (an older run) lists 8,925 complexes across these 8 provinces. (a8.py)

findings.what: Province assignment and grid cells differ slightly from the platform. The deck uses the simplified public/geo/provinsi.json (e.g. Kalteng has 451 vertices); the platform's wilayah.Wilayah uses the BIG kecamatan polygons. The deck's cell is (round(lon/G), round(lat/G)) without the platform's cos(lat) correction (harian.py pix(); laporan.py floor with 0.375/111.32). Each effect is ≤ ~1%.
findings.evidence:
Hotspot counts, deck vs platform polygons:
- Sumsel 18 Okt: 1,568 vs 1,561.
- Sulteng 20 Okt: 905 vs 911.
- Papua Selatan: 2,617 / 2,631 / 2,763 vs 2,619 / 2,632 / 2,766. The BNPB template had 2.618 / 2.632 / 2.766, so the platform polygons match BNPB more closely.

cos(8.5°) = 0.989. No holes, no overlaps, and no active-volcano points (Dempo / Kerinci / Kaba within 3 km) were found. (a6.py, a7.py)

result.summary:
The final deck matches angka.json exactly. My script ran 771 checks on slides 1-2 and none failed. The checks covered every hotspot, luas and belum label for the 8 provinces and 3 days; arrow text and colour against the previous day, with 17 Oct as the base for 18 Oct; bar colour matching its arrow; bar height within 1 EMU of max(18288, round(H*v/rowmax)) using H=201168 on slide 1 and 310896 on slide 2; '.' thousands formatting; and every totals row. Some results:
- Jumlah 5 provinsi: 15.855/6.776/4.601, 28.712/13.467/7.878, 18.475/10.820/5.235.
- Jumlah 3 provinsi: 3.941/3.770/4.426, 7.345/7.013/6.597, 4.371/3.504/3.251.
- Jumlah 8 provinsi equals the 5-province totals plus the 3-province totals: 19.796/10.546/9.027, 36.057/20.480/14.475, 22.846/14.324/8.486.
- The FS pills show 955/962/817, which equals the sum of fs over the 8 provinces.
- Slide 1 subtitle (±5.097, 49 persen, ±10.332, ±5.235) and slide 2's ±8.486 both match their formulas applied to angka.json. ±5.235 equals the slide 1 belum total for 20 Oct, and ±8.486 equals the slide 2 one.
- No old BNPB values are left on slides 1-2: none of NA, 497,09, 272/269/279 FS, 502,08, 983,34, 481,26, 554,76, TARGET or decimal-comma numbers.
- Slide 3 is byte-identical to the original (cmp found no difference).
- The minimum bar height clamp never applies.

I also recomputed the values from the raw FIRMS CSVs without rounding, using the same logic as hitung2.py. All angka.json values agree within 0.05. The problems come from rounding twice: hitung2.py stores luas, belum and padam rounded to 0.1, then ganti.py rounds them again for display and computes the arrows from the 0.1 values. That changes one displayed value, the slide 1 subtitle, three totals cells and four arrows (details in the findings). Bar heights are proportional to the 0.1 values rather than the displayed integers. The difference is at most about 1000 EMU (0.03 mm), so nobody can see it.

findings.what: Kalimantan Tengah BELUM PADAM 19 Okt shows 7.916 but the correctly rounded value is 7.917. The error carries into two totals rows.
findings.evidence: Exact value from raw data: (1064 N + 0.978*2677 N20)/2*4.3 = 7916.5279. angka.json stores it as 7916.5, and ganti.py's f0 uses Python round, which rounds .5 to the even number, giving 7916. Correctly rounded it is 7917. As a result, slide 1 'Jumlah 5 provinsi' BELUM 19 Okt shows 10.820 instead of 10.821, and slide 2 'Jumlah 8 provinsi' BELUM 19 Okt shows 14.324 instead of 14.325. The arrows are unaffected (▼42% on 19 Okt, ▼61% on 20 Okt).

findings.what: In the slide 1 subtitle, the 'telah padam' figure P and the total P+B are each 1 ha too high.
findings.evidence: Kalimantan Selatan padam on 20 Okt is exactly (278 N + 0.978*251 N20)/2*4.3 = 1125.4777, which should round to 1125. angka.json stores 1125.5, and round(1125.5) gives 1126. So P should be 3085+400+1125+73+413 = 5.096 and P+B = 10.331. The deck shows '±5.097 ha (49 persen) dari ±10.332 ha'. The percentage stays 49 (5096/10331 = 49.33%), and B = 5.235 is correct.

findings.what: Four arrow percentages are off by 1 point because they were computed from the 0.1-rounded angka.json values instead of the exact values.
findings.evidence:
- Jambi BELUM 19 Okt shows ▲12%. The exact change is 42.3851 to 47.2527 = 11.48%, so it should be ▲11%.
- Sulawesi Tengah LUAS 18 Okt shows ▲346%. The exact change is 100.0567 to 446.8646 = 346.61%, so ▲347%.
- Sulawesi Tengah LUAS 19 Okt shows ▲64%. The exact change is 446.8646 to 735.1280 = 64.51%, so ▲65%.
- Sulawesi Tengah BELUM 18 Okt shows ▲370%. The exact change is 21.2635 to 100.1513 = 371.00%, so ▲371%.

The arrow and bar colours are correct in all four cases.

findings.what: Some arrows do not match what a reader would calculate from the two numbers shown next to them. The spec allows this, since it does not say which values to use, but a reader may see it as an inconsistency.
findings.evidence:
- Jambi LUAS 20 Okt: shown 103 to 173 is +68%, but the arrow says ▲67%.
- Sumatera Selatan BELUM 20 Okt: shown 581 to 1.148 is +97.6%, but the arrow says ▲97%.
- Jambi BELUM 20 Okt: shown 47 to 81 is +72%, but the arrow says ▲71%.
- Kalimantan Timur BELUM 20 Okt: shown 991 to 471 is -52.5%, and the arrow says ▼53%.

The 18 Okt arrows (for example Kalsel belum ▲908%) cannot be checked by a reader at all, because the 17 Okt base is not on the slide.
